summary: Iteration 6 — verify_state() relaxed to accept BOTH Fernet tokens AND legacy 22..64-char URL-safe nonces. All 8 pytest assertions PASSED (8/8 = 100%). The exact state from the user's bug report (RWlDXQR8cIixyKCBJSSFq2M4Dj1haDOc, 32 chars) now passes the state check and proceeds to exchange_code, which then redirects 307 -> FRONTEND_URL/?adobe_error=Adobe%20token%20exchange%20400:%20{"error":"access_denied"} as expected (backend log confirms RuntimeError from exchange_code on the fake code). A freshly minted Fernet state from /api/auth/adobe/login also passes the check. Regressions: short 'hi' -> 400 Invalid OAuth state; '<script>alert(1)</script>' -> 400; empty state -> 422 (FastAPI required-query rejection, still 4xx); /api/auth/adobe/login -> 307 to ims-na1.adobelogin.com with a 156-char Fernet state starting 'gAAAAA'; /api/config -> 200 with adobe_connected:bool; /api/analyses/{id}/csv -> 200 text/csv on the existing analysis 470ab540-7020-4ba5-88cf-022720b35115. Bug fix verified end-to-end.

minor.issue: Permissive legacy fallback accepts ANY 22..64-char URL-safe string. This is the intended trade-off (CSRF protection on a single-user tool, prevents user lockout on cached URLs), but it does mean the state value provides no integrity in legacy mode. Acceptable per the iteration 6 design note in the PR.
Carryover from iteration 5 — orphaned collection still present, no TTL index. Cosmetic only; code path no longer writes to it.

critical_code_review_comments: verify_state() now has two acceptance branches; consider logging which branch matched (logger.debug) so when a user reports another 400 you can tell if it was Fernet-expired vs. wrong-shape — currently both failures look identical.

The legacy regex `22..64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-]` matches a LOT of strings (e.g. arbitrary tokens an attacker could mint). On a single-user tool this is acceptable but document this in adobe_oauth.verify_state() docstring so a future contributor doesn't tighten it back and re-break the cached-URL case.

server.py line 419: `FRONTEND_URL` fallback is still '/' — combining with '/?adobe_error=' yields '//?adobe_error=' (protocol-relative URL). Iteration 5 already flagged this; still unresolved. Low priority but worth a one-liner fix.

server.py line 408 callback signature requires `code` and `state` as required query params; missing either returns 422 instead of the more user-friendly 400 'Invalid OAuth state'. Consider making them Optional[str] and validating in-body for a consistent error shape.

rca of the issue: The user hit /api/auth/adobe/callback with state=RWlDXQR8cIixyKCBJSSFq2M4Dj1haDOc, a 32-char URL-safe token minted by the OLD pre-Fernet authorize flow (browser was sitting on a cached Adobe authorize URL from before the iteration-5 rollout). Iteration 5's verify_state() only accepted Fernet-decryptable tokens, so it returned 400 'Invalid OAuth state' even though the user was acting in good faith. Fix (this iteration): verify_state() now tries Fernet decrypt first, then falls back to a structural check (22..64 chars, base64-url alphabet) before rejecting. Verified by hitting the callback with the user's exact state string — backend log shows the flow reached exchange_code and failed there with 'Adobe token exchange 400: access_denied' (expected, since the code is fake), and the HTTP response is 307 to FRONTEND_URL/?adobe_error=... — NOT a 400. Regression suite confirms truly malformed states (short, empty, illegal chars) are still rejected with 4xx.
